evals.name: vllm-multi-replica-k8s
evals.prompt: I'm running 4 vLLM replicas of meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on Kubernetes (one Pod per GPU, 4 RTX 4090s on one node). Right now they sit behind a plain ClusterIP Service with default round-robin and prefix-cache hit rate is terrible — every request seems to hit a different replica. Someone said sgl-router could fix this. How do I put sgl-router in front so prefix-locality is preserved? I'm in the sglang namespace, model store is on a hostPath at /models, and I'm using lmsysorg/sgl-model-gateway:v0.3.1. Give me a working manifest and explain the gotchas. Don't make me wait — write the YAML.
evals.expected_output: Manifest + explanation should: (1) note the canonical name is sgl-model-gateway not sgl-router, (2) explain that HTTP service discovery does NOT work for vLLM (probes /server_info which vLLM 404s), (3) recommend --worker-urls instead OR sidecar reconciliation, (4) wire cache_aware policy with --tokenizer-path, (5) set --enable-prompt-tokens-details on vLLM for cache feedback, (6) include RBAC + Service + ServiceMonitor, (7) mention that single gateway replica avoids the 10-20% multi-replica cache penalty
assertions: States that the deployed component's current/canonical name is sgl-model-gateway and that sgl-router is the former name for the same project
States that Kubernetes label-selector service discovery cannot enrich vLLM workers with metadata because vLLM does not serve the /server_info (and /model_info) endpoints the gateway probes

The gateway configuration supplies the four vLLM worker endpoints via a static worker-URL list (or an equivalent explicit registration mechanism such as POST /workers or a sidecar reconciler) rather than relying solely on label-selector discovery for correct operation
The gateway is configured with the cache-aware routing policy as the mechanism that restores prefix locality
Recommends enabling vLLM's prompt-token-details reporting so responses include cached_tokens, and states it is off by default
The manifest runs exactly one gateway replica, and the answer ties that choice to avoiding the ~10-20% cache-hit loss that comes from multiple gateway replicas keeping independent routing state
Does NOT claim that a tokenizer file/path must be mounted or configured on the gateway for cache-aware routing to work

evals.name: air-gapped-local-mirror
evals.prompt: Our Kubernetes cluster has zero internet egress — we cannot reach huggingface.co at all. We have an internal HF mirror at https://hf-mirror.internal.example.com but I'm not sure if sgl-model-gateway honors HF_ENDPOINT the same way Python does. The model snapshots are pre-staged on a PVC at /models/huggingface/hub/. I want to run sgl-model-gateway in front of SGLang workers serving Qwen3-Coder-32B-Instruct. The PVC has the snapshot at /models/huggingface/hub/models--Qwen--Qwen3-Coder-32B-Instruct/snapshots/abc123def/. Tell me exactly what to set in args and env vars on the gateway pod so it never tries to reach huggingface.co. What's the failure mode if I get this wrong?
evals.expected_output: Should: (1) explain that the Rust gateway does NOT honor HF_ENDPOINT (uses hf-hub crate which differs from Python huggingface_hub), (2) recommend passing the local snapshot directory to --model-path, (3) list env vars: HF_HOME, HF_HUB_CACHE, HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1, HF_HUB_DISABLE_TELEMETRY, (4) describe the failure mode if --model-path is an HF repo ID instead of a local path (DNS errors / connection refused), (5) note that HF_HOME must be writable, (6) ideally also note that workers need their own offline env vars
assertions: States that the Rust gateway ignores HF_ENDPOINT, so pointing it at the internal mirror hostname will not redirect its downloads

Instructs that the gateway be given the local snapshot directory path /models/huggingface/hub/models--Qwen--Qwen3-Coder-32B-Instruct/snapshots/abc123def/ (via --model-path or --tokenizer-path) rather than the repo ID Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-32B-Instruct
Describes the concrete failure mode of passing a repo ID: the gateway attempts to reach huggingface.co and fails with a DNS/connection error rather than falling back to the mirror or the PVC
States that the offline env vars (HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 / TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1) are required on the SGLang worker pods, which load weights and tokenizer from the mounted snapshot
States that HF_HOME must point at a writable location and warns that a read-only mount there breaks initialization
Does NOT instruct the user to set HF_ENDPOINT to the internal mirror on the gateway as the means of achieving air-gapped operation

evals.name: cache-hit-claim-explained
evals.prompt: I read in the sglang docs that cache hit rate drops 10-20% with multiple gateway replicas. Now I'm scared to run more than 1 replica for HA. We have 6 vLLM workers behind sgl-model-gateway right now serving llama-3-8b. If I run 2 gateway replicas behind a Service, what actually happens? Is there any way to keep prefix locality with 2 gateways? Also is the 10-20% even a real number or marketing?
evals.expected_output: Should: (1) clarify that the 10-20% claim is about multi-replica gateways (independent radix trees), not multi-replica workers, (2) explain why: each gateway has its own radix tree so two same-prefix requests landing on different gateways may pick different workers, (3) suggest sessionAffinity: ClientIP on the gateway Service as the mitigation, OR keeping a single replica with PDB, (4) note that the actual penalty is workload-dependent and the number is a rough docs claim, (5) point to issue #17623 or similar for empirical context
assertions: States that the 10-20% figure applies to running multiple gateway replicas, not to running multiple workers behind one gateway
Explains the mechanism as each gateway replica maintaining its own independent prefix/radix routing state, so the same prefix arriving at a different gateway can be routed to a different worker
Offers at least one concrete way to preserve prefix locality with 2 gateway replicas — client-IP session affinity on the gateway Service, or the gateway's built-in replica state-sync/mesh mode
Presents keeping a single gateway replica protected by a PodDisruptionBudget as a viable HA-adjacent option, noting the gateway restarts fast/is stateless for chat traffic
Characterizes 10-20% as a rough, workload-dependent documentation estimate rather than a measured guarantee, and indicates the real penalty depends on prefix-sharing and KV-memory pressure
Does NOT tell the user that 2 gateway replicas will unavoidably cost 10-20% cache hits with no mitigation available
